draft.title: Urbanisation
card: Urban growth
Urban growth is cities getting bigger, in population or in area. It is a head count or a size, such as a city rising from 2 million to 3 million people.
Urbanisation
Urbanisation is the growing share of a country's people who live in cities and towns. It is measured as a percentage, not as a head count.
Set side by side
Cities can grow without urbanisation if rural areas grow at the same rate. Urbanisation means the urban share goes up, so the rural share goes down.
Why cities grow
Cities often grow when people move in from rural areas for jobs, services and education. Natural increase in cities adds to the growth as well.
draft.remember: Urban growth is a bigger city. Urbanisation is a rising urban share.

a.q: Which change in a country is an example of urbanisation?
opts: Urban share of people rises from 50% to 60%
Urban and rural populations both grow by 10%
Rural share of people rises from 40% to 50%
Urban and rural populations both fall by 5%
a.why: Urbanisation is a rising urban share, so a move from 50% to 60% shows it. If urban and rural populations both grow by 10%, cities get bigger but the urban share stays the same, so there is no urbanisation.
a.clue: Compare the people in cities with the whole population.

b.q: Country X grew from 10 million to 12 million people. Its city dwellers grew from 5 million to 6 million. What does this show?
opts: Urban growth, but no urbanisation, as the share stayed at 50%
Urbanisation, as the urban population grew by a million
Urbanisation, as the total population grew by 2 million
Neither, as the city population did not get any bigger
b.why: City dwellers rose from 5 to 6 million, so there was urban growth. The urban share was 5 ÷ 10 = 50% and then 6 ÷ 12 = 50%. The share did not change, so there was no urbanisation.
b.clue: Check the city head count, then the urban share.

proposal.title: Urban growth and urbanisation
card: Urban growth
cities getting bigger, in population or in area. It is measured as a count or a size, such as a city rising from 2 million to 3 million people.
Urbanisation
a rising share of a country's people living in urban areas (cities and towns) rather than rural areas. It is measured as a percentage.
Urban share = city population ÷ total population × 100. For example, 3 million city dwellers out of 4 million people is 75%.
Cities can grow without urbanisation if rural areas grow at the same rate. Urbanisation means the urban share goes up, so the rural share goes down.
proposal.remember: Urban growth is a bigger city. Urbanisation is a bigger urban share.
